newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Tranz Rail sets dividend, plans upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Tranz Rail sets dividend, plans upgrades.

text.p: New Zealand rail and ferry operator Tranz Rail Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it would pay a dividend of 17 NZ cents/share on March 14.
The dividend will be 31.2 percent imputed, with imputations credits totalling NZ$9.7 million. Shareholders registered at March 7 will be eligible.
Tranz Rail said the dividend was intended to be for the full year and no further dividend was expected in 1997.

The company announced separately that it would add a new ferry to its fleet between the North and South Islands by the end of 1998. The ferry, about the size of the largest current ferry Arahura, will be able to carry up to 350 passengers and their cars as well as trucks and rail wagons.

The ferry, for which negotiations on price and delivery date are under way with two European yards, will be able to berth at the existing South Island terminal at Picton and the proposed new terminal at Clifford Bay.
Tranz Rail said it was considering a NZ$565 million investment over the next 11 years to provide a new inter-island fleet and new North and South Island terminals.
The company said it would also invest NZ$28 million to upgrade its Christchurch rail yard and freight handling facilities.
Tranz Rail is 22.7 percent owned by Wisconsin Central Transportation Corp.
